articles.title: Squash and chickpea curry, and whipped beans with radicchio: Marie Mitchell’s sweet-and-sour recipes
articles.description: Pucker up for squash and tamarind curry with stewed chickpeas and coriander, or how about whipped cannellini beans with leeks, roast radicchio and parmesan? Who doesn’t love sweet and sour? If you’re complaining that you don’t right now, then you’re lying – it’s an almost perfect pairing. Here, I’m playing with the sweet-and-sour notes of vinegar and the tang of tamarind in two dishes that are on repeat in our house. Dinners for when you want to spend more time on the sofa and less time in the kitchen. Continue reading...

articles.title: Michael by Bob Mortimer review – heartwarming quirkiness from the comedian
articles.description: Mortimer’s off-kilter charm energises the story of a troubled teenager in 1970s Middlesbrough In comedian Bob Mortimer’s fourth novel, Michael, when we meet him, isn’t an angel; but he’s in a place that he suspects is at least angel-adjacent. He’s dead, or close to it, having come round from an emergency heart bypass in his 52nd year only to find himself sinking into a deep pool of warm gloop with honey-coloured light flowing at him from all directions. A disembodied voice calling itself Charles has offered him a choice that is hinted at but so far unspecified. What we do know is that before he makes his choice, Michael – a rock star who had three Top 10 hits in the UK and once danced in an LA disco with Björk and Courtney Love – is invited to revisit a single year of his life. He lands, somewhat trepidatiously, on the year he turned 14. So back down memory lane we amble, the mysterious and otherworldly frame story intruding only in brief chapters now and again, recounting our hero’s comically tetchy exchanges with Charles. Here, really, is a sweet coming-of-age story with a delicate frosting of It’s a Wonderful Life. Continue reading...

articles.title: Souped-up and now on screen, Starlight Express is moving in all sorts of ways
articles.description: Luke Sheppard’s revival of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s 80s musical is in cinemas and going on tour. What gives these ridiculous, rollerskating trains such emotional force? I hardly ever cry at the theatre but can think of three recent cases. 1. The beautifully jittery balcony scene in Liverpool Everyman’s Romeo and Juliet . 2. Dear Theodosia as co-sung by Leslie Odom Jr (actual OG Aaron Burr!) in Hamilton . 3. An embarrassingly large amount of Starlight Express . Why on earth does this ridiculous fantasy of rollerskating trains, with their high-speed scrapes, leave me feeling like an emotional wreck? That’s what happened when I first saw director Luke Sheppard’s souped-up London revival – and again this month, watching a new film of that production. Continue reading...

articles.title: Jess Elliott Dennison’s quick and easy recipe for ricotta dumplings with sage butter, rocket and lemon | Quick and easy
articles.description: Easy cheesy dumplings with the perfect level of lightness and squidge Making gnocchi from scratch can be a bit of a faff midweek. However, these ricotta-and-parmesan-based dumplings are so easy to throw together, and always come out light and with just the right amount of squidge. Sage and brown butter feels the right sauce at this time of year, but you could serve them with a simple tomato sauce instead. Any leftover dumplings work a treat thrown into a brothy, minestrone-type soup. Continue reading...

articles.title: I Am Helen review – Nicola Coughlan is absolutely superb in this terrifying must-watch
articles.description: After the week we’ve had, you may not feel ready to watch this brilliantly powerful film about the toxic manosphere and its impact on relationships. But do make the time I would understand, after the week in the news we’ve had, if you were not feeling quite ready to deal with the new instalment of I Am … , Dominic Savage’s anthology series that examines different aspects of women’s lives and tends to do so with merciless precision and in pitiless detail. The stories are worked out with the female actor central to each: Vicky McClure in 2019’s inaugural I Am Nicola, about coercive control, Samantha Morton in one about the vulnerabilities poverty brings, Suranne Jones imploding under the accumulated pressures of midlife and trying to be everything to everyone because nobody else will pick up the slack, and other heavy hitters like Lesley Manville and Kate Winslet starring with younger actors to showcase different generational concerns. The latest was devised with Nicola Coughlan. Continue reading...

articles.title: Don’t wait for a change in the age of consent. Adults can act to stop age-gap abuse | Gaby Hinsliff
articles.description: The law is important, but so is the fact that people know when associates embark on inappropriate relationships. They bear responsibility too Mia Latter was 16 and out clothes-shopping when Russell Brand stopped her on the street. He riffled through her bags to choose a dress he told her she should wear for the date he’d be taking her on. And so began a short relationship – if that’s the right word, given she was still at school and he was a 30-year-old MTV presenter, who she says publicly referred to her as “the child”. Towards the end, she claims, Brand orally raped her . Lilly Creightmore was 18 when she says the then 32-year-old celebrity David Walliams asked her to dinner and then began pestering her for sex. There’s a hauntingly awkward photograph of her with him at a celebrity bash. Another time, at a house party, a fellow guest remembers her sitting on the floor alone, like a bored child. She now feels his behaviour was an abuse of power over someone vulnerable. Walliams’s lawyers say he denies grooming her or behaving inappropriately. Gaby Hinsliff is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

articles.title: Russia, Saudi Arabia and Australia named as biggest CO2 exporters in history
articles.description: Analysis of fossil fuel exports since 1850 differs from most assessments – which look at countries where CO 2 is released Russia, Saudi Arabia and Australia are the three biggest exporters of carbon dioxide in history, according to analysis of fossil fuels since 1850. Russia tops the list of global exporters of fossil fuels, with its vast coal, oil and gas deposits. Accounting for the CO 2 produced by burning these exports, Russia has been responsible for almost 70 gigatonnes, up to the end of 2025. Continue reading...

articles.title: Rocky is Philadelphia’s founding myth – and 50 years later, we’re still telling it
articles.description: As Sylvester Stallone’s Oscar-winning drama celebrates its 50th anniversary, I Play Rocky helps to further turn the boxing hero into the stuff of legend The story behind the making of Rocky has always sounded uncannily like Rocky itself. An unknown with an improbable dream, a skeptical establishment and a refusal to accept the odds: Sylvester Stallone’s real-life struggle to crack the industry and bring his breakthrough film to the screen contained all the elements of the underdog story he sought to tell. Now, half a century later, Peter Farrelly’s I Play Rocky has crafted those parallels into a crowd-pleasing yarn of its own. It’s an extraordinary afterlife for a modest boxing flick that became the highest-grossing film of 1976 on a $1m budget and won the Oscar for best picture over one of the most stacked fields in history. Yet its greatest achievement may be the durability of the story – dismissed then by the New York Times as a “sentimental little slum movie” and Gene Siskel as a “flatout schmaltzy saga” – that we’re still finding new ways to repurpose all these years later through six Rocky films, three Creed sequels, a Broadway musical , and too many documentaries, novelizati

articles.title: The corporate boom in vegan food is dead. Long live real plant-based cooking | Isobel Lewis
articles.description: The fad for plant-based junk food has run its course, but restaurants reflecting the centuries-long history of this cuisine still thrive Have you ever gone to make a restaurant reservation and been met with a Google Maps listing bearing that harbinger of doom: “Permanently closed”? It’s a pretty deflating feeling – and one the UK’s vegan population knows well. Over the past few years, many once-beloved, plant-based establishments have shut up shop or moved away from brick-and-mortar businesses, from The Allotment in Manchester to The Vurger Co, which had restaurants in London and Brighton. Each shuttering galvanises the vegan community into supporting their local spots. But they’re gutting too, and deeply felt by a group who see themselves more as an ethically motivated community than simply clientele. The so-called sorry state of the vegan restaurant scene has been widely reported on (not least by me ). But after working with the food magazine Vittles on its inaugural London vegan guide , I have begun to challenge the “death of vegan dining” narrative that I had found myself perpetuating. And yes, a depressing number of my choices for the Vegan 99 closed while I was writing it; mo

articles.title: Former WH Smith chain TG Jones put up for sale after closing 130 stores
articles.description: Modella Capital plans auction of high street retailer, which employs about 3,500 people, next year The owner of TG Jones is exploring a potential sale less than 18 months after completing a deal to buy the high street chain formerly known as WH Smith. Modella Capital, which also owns businesses including Hobbycraft, completed a deal to buy the 233-year-old business for £42m in June last year. Continue reading...

articles.title: The Brightness by Chad Harbach review – an ambitious sequel to The Art of Fielding
articles.description: Fifteen years on, this expansive follow-up to the campus epic explores female agency, friendship – and the messiness of early adulthood Back in 2011, Chad Harbach’s debut The Art of Fielding was hailed as the next Great American Novel. Set on the campus of Westish, a fictional midwestern liberal arts college, and steeped in baseball, it grappled with the big, quintessentially American themes – ambition, failure, the pursuit of perfection – that have traditionally been the genre’s hallmark. Harbach himself winkingly invited the categorisation: The Art of Fielding communes directly with the spirit of Herman Melville, arguably the greatest Great American Novelist of them all. Westish College, the novel explains, has claimed Melville as its own since the discovery of a lecture he gave there in 1880: its baseball team is known as the Harpooners; and a Melville statue presides over the campus like the genius of the place. Legend has it that Harbach laboured over The Art of Fielding for more than a decade. When it finally emerged, a feverish bidding war saw it sell for more than $650,000 (£431,000), a saga chronicled at length in Vanity Fair. Any follow-up to such a high-profile debut, le

articles.title: The play that changed my life: ‘John Berger’s Pig Earth became something magical – they licked milk off bodies’
articles.description: The Three Lives of Lucie Cabrol by Complicité conjured the struggles of a French village with an intense rawness There are many things you see that are impactful, but few you can genuinely say change your life. I saw Complicité’s The Three Lives of Lucie Cabrol aged 16 on a school trip to Riverside Studios in London and it really reached me. I’d been educated in a very language, words-based way. Here the story was told – with such intensity! – through people’s bodies. The world they were conjuring, from a story by John Berger in his book Pig Earth, was about this remote French village – a world of labour. And the strife and struggles of these characters was expressed through the physical work of the company. Continue reading...

articles.title: Sami Tamimi’s recipes for lamb and quince tagine with maftoul
articles.description: Falling-apart-tender lamb with jewelled, nutty bulgur wheat is a riot of texture and flavour These dishes were made to sit together. The lamb is slowly cooked with quince and saffron, bringing richness, warmth and a gentle sweetness, while the maftoul offers a lighter contrast with its lemon, currants and toasted almonds, and provides the perfect base for the fragrant meat juices. It’s a generous combination; simple enough for a family meal, but special enough to share with friends. Continue reading...

articles.title: Neet ideas: what’s in Alan Milburn’s report on young people not in education, employment or training?
articles.description: Former minister’s 278-page report calls for changes to employment regulations, education, healthcare and benefits Who are the Neets? UK youth job crisis in five charts Milburn urges Burnham to spend billions on young people Five months on from a first report detailing the growing crisis of young people who are not in education, employment or training (Neet), Alan Milburn has produced his recommendations on how to tackle it. Set out over 278 pages, they amount to, as he readily accepts, a major rethink of everything from employment regulations to education, healthcare and benefits. Here is what he has said. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘Mick Jagger should fold up his penis and go home’: the caustic genius of music critic Robert Christgau
articles.description: Beloved for his savage takedowns and rhapsodic raves, the legendary Village Voice reviewer opens up in a candid new documentary Rows and rows of CDs, albums, cassettes and books creak and groan on shelves that snake around the walls and choke the halls of an apartment in New York City’s East Village. The clutter that sprawls through its rooms is so dense it suggests the twistiest parts of a Moroccan medina or a warren no self-respecting rabbit would allow. Buried amid the muddle is a man hunched over a computer keyboard, clacking out words meant to make sense of all the sounds that these physical media hold. Welcome to the lair of Robert Christgau, the self-declared “Dean of American Rock Critics”, as seen in a new documentary provocatively titled The Last Critic . “Bob is someone who has probably listened to more music, and published more words about music, than anyone to walk the face of the earth, and he’s still doing it in his mid-80s,” says Matty Wishnow, who directed the film. “It’s a career that’s both unprecedented and unrepeatable.” Continue reading...

articles.title: I got scammed on Instagram – and it led to a truly disgusting dinner | Zoe Williams
articles.description: Intrigued by an unusual recipe for spinach tacos, I followed the instructions, but was left with a soggy, inedible mess. It turns out there are a lot of made-up meals out there I can’t tell you when my Instagram algorithm changed, from – this is embarrassing, but what the hell – buff guys trying to exercise and being interrupted by a Staffordshire bull terrier who wants to help them exercise, to cooking videos, but it has. I now get endless food content, following the same format: a millennial has 20 minutes to make dinner for his or her beloved (it’s very gender neutral), and launches into some unlikely techniques. He might shove a load of chicken into a cake tin, sprinkle mismatched spices all over, bake it, then slice it, as if it were a cake. Or she might cook tagliatelle in a pan of milk and salmon. This is not how it’s done, I think, as I watch all the way to the end, and then am astonished to be fed yet more weird food content. Drawn with an almost zombified lack of free will, I got the yen to try it for myself. What would happen if you boiled a white cabbage whole, then roasted it in honey and miso? Well, I can tell you: the cabbage is very soft on the outside, and still un

articles.title: Bows and old guns: Indigenous militias left to fight Peru’s cocaine gangs alone
articles.description: Decades after Lima armed them to fight Shining Path rebels, the Asháninka are still defending their Amazon rainforest, but now against drug traffickers – and without any help Shielding his eyes from the tropical sun, Irmeo Sánchez Gómez – better known by his nom de guerre, Kiri – pointed up at a weathered shed on top of a hill, a few frayed sandbags piled at its base. Beyond it, the Tambo River snaked through Peru’s Amazonian rainforest. “When the terrorists came,” Kiri says, “they would shoot up at us from the riverbank. Without guns of our own, we defended ourselves with bows and arrows. Later, the army gave us guns and built these defences.” Continue reading...

articles.title: Anti-Trump protests in Manila and a red crab migration: photos of the day – Tuesday
articles.description: The Guardian’s picture editors select photographs from around the world Continue reading...

articles.title: Robert Pattinson’s gift for cool, sensual menace makes him an exquisite choice as James Bond | Peter Bradshaw
articles.description: Pattinson is a character actor whose talent for inscrutable appraisal may mean a new era for 007. Will this more willowy, classy Bond leave sexism in the shadows? • New James Bond announced ... and the name’s Pattinson, Robert Pattinson • Share your thoughts on the casting • Pattinson’s journey from Harry Potter and Twilight to James Bond If it wasn’t Bond … maybe it would have been Dr No in some hi-tech reboot. But Robert Pattinson – with his movie-star chops and track record in hip A24-type character turns, and his gift for cool, inscrutable appraisal and sensual menace – is an exquisite choice as 007, playing on the darker and more sophisticated notes of Pattinson’s performing personality. And let’s hope, incidentally, that the actor now isn’t forced into a five-hour daily gym regimen to bulk up. I like the taller and more willowy Bond that Pattinson represents, the Bond from whose frame the tux hangs gracefully, the Bond with elegant abandon who’s a former British Naval officer, not a former US Navy Seal, the Bond who with a crinkly-eyed reptilian grin can style out waking up with a hangover after too many whisky-and-sodas at the baccarat table. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘We are all in’: the Democrats trying to turn round the US’s reputation at Cop31
articles.description: The 120-strong America Is All In group are trying to ensure that the US won’t remained sidelined at the climate talks for very much longer. Plus: wild oysters are back in Scotland and a super El Niño looms over Cop • Don’t get Down to Earth delivered to your inbox? Sign up here The final week of Cop31 is in full swing, with just four days left to set a broad range of climate commitments into concrete action. I am on the ground at this year’s UN annual climate summit, where thousands of world leaders, businesses, nonprofits and scientists have converged in Antalya, Turkey, and there’s a lot left to do as the clock ticks down. “Nearly 200 countries are working through 165 mandates,” executive secretary Simon Stiell told reporters at the midpoint on Saturday, pushing for a swift move to the hardest issues and championing compromise. “Each country has a view,” he said. “Every country has a voice.” European-made pesticides named in 1,605 poisoning reports in Brazil last year AI models ‘weak and fallible’ on climate science, UN-backed study reports ‘I was home alone when the glacier collapsed. My mum called and told me to run’ Continue reading...

articles.title: Age instead of need drives Alan Milburn’s new reforms. Welcome to the two-tier welfare state | Frances Ryan
articles.description: The long-awaited plan to address youth unemployment in the UK has positive aspects, but it will cause huge anxiety for young people with disabilities Continue reading...

articles.title: Milburn’s absurdly ambitious report offers blueprint for fixing everything and everyone
articles.description: He lays out sweeping aims and finer details for how to fix the Neets crisis – and is obsessive about welfare Neet ideas: what’s in Milburn’s report? It is not clear if too many people were expecting Everything Everywhere All at Once, but that is what Alan Milburn has delivered. From a Welfare State to a Working State is almost absurdly ambitious. The terms of reference said something about the drivers of youth labour markets. We got a blueprint for how to fix everything and everyone. What Keir Starmer, who commissioned it, had in mind, we’ll never know, but Milburn has taken up with gusto Andy Burnham’s general invocation to think boldly and rewire the state. Yes, it’s about training and jobs, but it’s also about pulling apart the NHS, giving schools and colleges an MOT, and once again, blowing up old-fashioned social security . Continue reading...

articles.title: Milburn calls for tax cuts for businesses hiring young people despite union concerns
articles.description: Youth unemployment review risks clash with unions and Labour left over workers’ rights and minimum wage Neet ideas: what’s in Alan Milburn’s youth unemployment report? Who are the Neets? UK youth job crisis in five charts Milburn urges Burnham to spend billions on young people Alan Milburn has called on ministers to cut business taxes and ease regulations to encourage employers to hire more young people, setting up a potential clash with trade unions and the Labour left over employment rights. The former health secretary published the results of his year-long review into youth unemployment on Wednesday, in what the prime minister, Andy Burnham, called a “watershed moment” for young people. Continue reading...

articles.title: New UK-EU youth mobility scheme may not fully launch until 2030
articles.description: Exclusive: deal expected to be sealed in principle at EU-UK summit on Friday but trickier elements could be postponed for six months The new post-Brexit UK-EU youth mobility scheme may not come fully into force until 2030. It will be a disappointment to any under-30s in the UK and the EU who hoped to travel, work or study in each other’s territories from next year after the long-awaited new deal. Continue reading...

articles.title: Using law to try to silence abuse victims is ‘ultimate form of gaslighting’, MPs told
articles.description: Woman sued by alleged rapist tells justice committee that Slapp lawsuits present perpetrator as victim of wrongdoing Attempts by perpetrators and alleged perpetrators of sexual abuse to silence their victims using the law are “the ultimate form of gaslighting”, MPs have heard. Verity Nevitt, a co-founder of the Gemini Project , a survivor-led nonprofit organisation, told the House of Commons justice committee about the ordeal of being sued by the man she and her sister, Lucy, respectively accused of sexual abuse and rape. Continue reading...

articles.title: American soldier held in UK suspected of spying for Russia taken into US military custody
articles.description: Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner was arrested by British police on 10 November over allegations related to espionage A US soldier who was arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia has been taken into custody by the US military, police have said. Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner, 41, was detained by British counter-terrorism police ‌on 10 November in Gloucestershire over allegations relating ⁠to espionage. Continue reading...

articles.title: Judge extends deadline for Trump’s deposition in $10bn BBC lawsuit
articles.description: President, who had agreed to sit for deposition in October but backed out, must now appear by 22 January Donald Trump has been granted a temporary delay before he must give a witness statement in his $10bn defamation lawsuit against the BBC. In late October, Enjoliqué Lett, a federal magistrate judge, gave Trump a firm 11 December deadline to sit for a deposition by lawyers representing the BBC in his lawsuit against the British broadcaster. If he failed to do so by that date, he could be subject to penalties up to dismissal of the case, the judge warned. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘Chloe’s policy’ aims to prevent repeat of case of Treasury worker who took her own life
articles.description: Exclusive: Parents of Chloe Moffat urge employers to treat staff facing allegations in a kinder, more human way The parents of a Treasury worker who took her own life last year have launched a policy that directs employers to treat staff in a kinder and more commonsense way, and are asking HR departments across the country to adopt it. Chloe Moffat’s parents also said the government department plans to plant a memorial garden in her honour at its Horse Guards Road offices. In the UK and Ireland, Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. In the US, you can call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org . In Australia, the crisis support service Lifeline is 13 11 14. Other international helplines can be found at befrienders.org Continue reading...

articles.title: Wayne Rooney says he contemplated taking own life during playing career
articles.description: Former England footballer opens up on mental health ‘It was probably the lowest point’ at Manchester United Wayne Rooney has revealed there was a period in his Manchester United career where he contemplated taking his own life. The former England striker said that, even as he flourished on the pitch, he was struggling with his mental health off it, despite being newly married and a dad to his eldest child, Kai. He said he would spend two days at a time drinking at home and, he told the Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast, at his lowest point considered taking his own life. Continue reading...

articles.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping review – surreally awful prequel to the Katniss Everdeen era
articles.description: Overwrought and boring, this nadir of a prequel to the Games’ death match saga is nothing but a cash grab for an exhausted franchise Here is yet another iteration of the utterly exhausted, unbearably extended and now surreally boring Hunger Games franchise, based on the YA bestsellers by Suzanne Collins. This one has another of the series’ convoluted faux-mythic subtitles: Sunrise on the Reaping. What, “harvest dawn” not old-timey enough? Well, “reaping” in fact refers to an annual process by which ordinary smudgy faced, raggedy clothed people are chosen at random for compulsory participation in this futurist dystopia’s brutal, televised survival contest to the death: a bread-and-circuses nightmare with which the rulers keep the populace in a cowed and pacified state. In this Darwinian process, competitors strategically team up with (and then betray) some players against others in the short term, to stay in the game. Continue reading...

articles.title: Spud-one-likes: is King Charles really a baked potato aficionado?
articles.description: On a visit to Preston, the royal revealed his favourite classic filling. But with jacket potatoes as far as the eye could see, he surprisingly failed to order one ... Name: Jacket potatoes. Age: As everyone knows, potatoes originated in South America where Incas cooked them in a huatia, an oven dug in the earth. So quite ancient. Continue reading...

articles.title: Is Robert Pattinson the right choice for James Bond? - The Latest
articles.description: It’s official: Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond. The British actor is known for leading roles in the Hollywood franchises Twilight, The Batman and Dune. Pattinson entered the race for Bond at a relatively late stage, beating earlier frontrunners including Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor. With 007’s identity confirmed, what will the new Bond era look like? Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian’s film editor, Catherine Shoard Continue reading...

articles.title: Where do people want to see Britain’s climate action plan working? On their own doorstep | Miatta Fahnbulleh
articles.description: I am at Cop31 – concerned about the crisis around the world, but mindful that voters want jobs, warmer homes and cheaper prices Miatta Fahnbulleh is the UK secretary of state for energy security and net zero In this cold weather, it is easy to forget that Britain has just been through its hottest summer on record, part of our new reality as the climate crisis reaches our doorstep. For millions around the world, the consequences have already been more devastating for the communities that did the least to cause this crisis. That is the backdrop to Cop31 in Antalya, Turkey, where I arrive on Tuesday as the UK’s chief negotiator. As I have prepared for these negotiations, I’ve been reflecting on the gap between the science and the political debate in Britain. Early predictions by the Met Office indicate that 2027 will surpass 2024 as the hottest year on record globally as El Niño rips through the Pacific. This is a sobering reality. And yet, the Conservatives and Reform UK want to bury their heads in the sand and break the consensus on delivering net zero. But we know sustained climate action can work. Continue reading...

articles.title: Hoping for Britain to rejoin the EU with Andy Burnham? You may be waiting a long time | Timothy Garton Ash
articles.description: The PM’s first big speech on the UK and Europe was cautious and disappointing. Don’t expect any great leaps towards a new deal Ever since Andy Burnham became the British prime minister this summer, people all over Europe have been asking me one question: “Will the UK rejoin the EU?” Sometimes they add: “And if so, when?” None of the intermediate options between the current hard Brexit and Brejoin are of any interest at all to most other Europeans. Measured against these great expectations, Burnham’s first big speech on Britain and Europe, delivered on Monday evening amid all the pomp and circumstance the City of London could furnish, must be considered a disappointment. It was both a cautious and a curiously old-fashioned speech. Continue reading...

articles.title: Should JD Vance run for president? I say go for it, habibi! | Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description: Now the vice-president’s luck is turning, he seems reluctant to commit himself to the next presidential race – and I, for one, hate to see it How do you think history will remember JD Vance? As the first vice-president to spark a vigorous debate about their eyeliner routine ? As one of the last public figures to see Pope Francis alive ? As the only politician in US history to have been the subject of a rumour about sexual relations with a couch (even though it was unfounded)? I have no idea. But it seems increasingly unlikely he will be remembered as the 48th president of the US. After Maga’s midterm thrashing, Vance’s political future doesn’t look as bright as it used to. So much so that there has been a flurry of recent headlines debating whether or not Vance, once considered Donald Trump’s heir apparent, may slink away from a presidential run altogether. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? If you would like to submit a response of up to 300 words by email to be considered for publication in our letters section, please click here . Continue reading...

articles.title: Portugal’s new No 7 Forbs channels Ronaldo for winner as Wales are denied
articles.description: One way or another, Portugal’s No 7 shirt has caused quite the commotion in recent weeks and months, if not years. Perhaps it was inevitable, then, that the first win of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era would come courtesy of the player wearing the updated jersey, one with a cross through the number to preserve Ronaldo’s eternal legacy, as the Portuguese Football Federation put it. A sumptuous finish by Carlos Forbs, a second-half substitute, was ultimately enough to clinch victory on a topsy-turvy night with Portugal surviving Pedro Neto’s sending-off for two yellow cards. For Wales, a Nations League relegation playoff double-header awaits in March, with Slovenia, Hungary, Republic of Ireland or Bosnia and Herzegovina – who knocked them out of World Cup qualifying this year – all potential opponents in Friday’s draw in Switzerland. Afterwards Craig Bellamy stressed the importance of keeping elite company to accelerate improvement but reiterated that he will not be in the job beyond Euro 2028, after which his contract expires. Continue reading...

articles.title: Rassie Erasmus’s tired ref-blaming act is wearing thin – South Africa deserve better | Robert Kitson
articles.description: Springboks’ achievements are remarkable but their head coach lacks statesmanship, diplomacy and good grace in defeat So here we go again. Exactly five years have passed since South Africa’s head coach, Rassie Erasmus, first felt the full force of World Rugby’s ire for criticising match officials. And guess what? This most habitual of offenders has just copped another lengthy ban – and deservedly so – for his latest intemperate comments, notable as ever for their total lack of statesmanship, diplomacy or good grace in defeat. To his acolytes his outspoken nature is part of what makes Rassie such a groot leier (great leader). To many others it simply cements his status as a serial prat. For the avoidance of any doubt everyone respects the remarkable achievements both of Erasmus and his double World Cup-winning teams. It is the rest of the package, sadly, that is too often a major letdown. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘The game is in danger’: PFA head Maheta Molango on Fifa, Infantino and football’s future
articles.description: At a potentially critical juncture for football, the PFA chief executive talks about the organisation, wider fears in the game and why the Folarin Balogun affair was ‘scandalous’ After five years in charge of the Professional Footballers’ Association, what has Maheta Molango learned? “The game is in danger,” the 43-year-old says. “I’ve learned that the game I loved and led me to first play and then advise and then lead a club and today to lead the PFA, is in danger because it is being forgotten.” In 2026, with football ubiquitous on all platforms, with a World Cup that generated $15bn (£11.4m) in revenue, and with attendances across the English pyramid growing year on year, it may seem hard to imagine forgetting about the game. But Molango’s unique perspective as head of the English players’ union observes a different picture; one where the future of the sport is being determined not by what will maintain its popularity, but what will make the most money. Continue reading...

articles.title: JJ Gabriel confirms Manchester United exit: ‘You gave me moments I will always treasure’
articles.description: Teenager says ‘thank you for everything’ in video Gabriel expected to join Real Madrid JJ Gabriel has announced his departure from Manchester United by posting a farewell message to the club on social media. The teenager, who has not played a competitive game for the first team, joined as a 10-year-old in 2020 but has been absent since he requested the cancellation of his registration in September before he turned 16, on 6 October. Continue reading...

articles.title: Zverev takes straight-sets win against Shelton in ATP Finals group stage – as it happened
articles.description: The world No 1 prevailed 6-2, 7-6 (4) in a rematch of the US Open final earlier this year, after Arthur Fils came from behind to beat Rafael Jódar Ready … play. Shelton’s backhand was pretty nifty against Arthur Fils in his first match. If it’s on tonight, he’s got a much better chance of winning – and it’s something Juan Carlos Ferrero must sort with him if he’s to improve on his current standing in the game. Continue reading...

articles.title: University of Birmingham pauses plans to move Shakespeare Institute after outcry
articles.description: Vice-chancellor halts proposed relocation from Stratford-upon-Avon but offers no guarantees over future The University of Birmingham has paused plans to move its much-loved Shakespeare Institute from Stratford-upon-Avon to its city campus after an outcry from scholars, actors and enthusiasts around the world. Prof Adam Tickell, the university’s vice-chancellor and principal, issued a statement on Tuesday evening saying proposals to relocate the institute and its renowned 60,000-volume library to the university’s Edgbaston campus would be put on hold while its future was explored. Continue reading...

articles.title: Isolated Brazilian tribe emerges amid alarm over threats to group’s way of life
articles.description: Indigenous Awá people of Amazon make contact with villagers and accept food to take back to territory About 20 Indigenous people emerged from isolation in Brazil’s Amazon rainforest, several organizations reported on Tuesday, raising the alarm about increased invasions into the tribe’s territory. According to the NGO Survival International, members of the Awá people, who live in voluntary isolation, arrived on Monday in a village and made contact with a government team in a “historic encounter”. Continue reading...

articles.title: Joy, hope and anger as Serbia student movement’s political novices enter parliament
articles.description: Celebrating supporters say they feel vindicated by arrival of Student List candidates in national assembly The paved plateau in front of Serbia’s national assembly became an impromptu dancefloor, as people of all ages joyfully whirled in a kolo. Drivers passing by sounded their horns, while hundreds of people waved flags, blew whistles and cheered. Every now and again, the crowd parted, allowing smartly dressed men and women to walk up the steps and into the building. These were the candidates from the Student List, on their way to being sworn in as members of parliament after their stunning victory in last month’s parliamentary elections . Those who had come to cheer them on displayed their feelings on badges, flags and placards. Continue reading...

articles.title: Anti-Arab hate speech surged on social media during Israel’s election, report finds
articles.description: Digital monitors recorded 400% rise in posts attacking Arab Israelis, including Netanyahu’s disproven fraud allegations Anti-Arab hate speech surged on social media in Israel around the country’s general election last month, digital monitors have said, as politicians including Benjamin Netanyahu levelled disproven allegations against Arab Israeli parties of election fraud. A new report by the Israel-based Brandeis Institute and FakeReporter recorded a deluge of anti-Arab discourse across social media platforms such as X, Facebook, Instagram and TikTok in the days surrounding Israel’s 27 October election. Continue reading...

articles.title: Costa Rican journalist shot dead in first such killing in 25 years
articles.description: Camilo Rodriguez’s death comes as the country grapples with a surge in drug violence The Costa Rican journalist Camilo Rodríguez, who gained prominence for publishing allegations against ⁠suspected drug traffickers and politicians, was shot dead on Monday, authorities said. articles.description: Claudia O’Doherty plays a chipper content creator dissociating through the apocalypse, in a 2019 web series that’s more relevant than ever Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email For most of her career, Australian actor and comedian Claudia O’Doherty has played on her adorable persona in the whimsical worlds of Bluey, Our Flag Means Death and Love, among others. She’s all big eyes and bangs, stealing scenes and hearts. But, as anyone who saw surprise hit Maddie’s Secret would know, O’Doherty is supremely satisfying as a villain. In John Early’s surreal yet oddly moving tale of a female food influencer’s battle with an eating disorder, O’Doherty broke bad as Maddie’s nemesis, Emily. articles.title: Pete Burgis obituary
articles.description: 0 My father, Pete Burgis, who has died aged 65, was an internationally acclaimed Foley artist whose work brought physical reality to films and television dramas. Foley – named after the pioneerng Warner Brothers sound engineer Jack Foley – is the art of creating sounds in sync with the picture, from footsteps and rustling clothes to the movements of creatures. Pete understood that these were not simply technical details but performances that could convey character, emotion and story . He won two Emmy awards, for Band of Brothers, in 2002, and Generation Kill, in 2009. Continue reading...

articles.title: The Last Spy review – a riveting tale of CIA meddling, espionage gossip and Blue Nun wine
articles.description: Refugee Peter Sichel was known as ‘the Jewish James Bond’ after fleeing Germany and becoming an integral cold war-era spy. He died last year but, at 100-years-old, he told his remarkable story for this film Why, exactly, was Peter Sichel “the last spy”? It’s not something Katharina Otto-Bernstein’s documentary about the cold war-era CIA man clarifies. The “Jewish James Bond” – as a woman from his synagogue nicknames him – is a catchier moniker, although that’s not quite right either. If Sichel was once a swashbuckling secret agent, we don’t hear much about his escapades here. Instead, he seems closer to M: sitting behind a desk pulling strings while his agents risked life and limb sneaking around the German Democratic Republic. The Last Spy begins as a straightforward but riveting biography built around a long, candid interview with Sichel, who was 100 at the time of filming (he died last year at 102). We hear about his childhood in Germany, which was initially privileged thanks to his great-grandfather’s lucrative wine business. articles.title: Ukraine is running out of time
articles.description: After over four-and-a-half years of entrenched warfare, reports of U.S.-backed peace talks to end Russia's war on Ukraine are back in the news. After Finland and Norway held Europe’s first direct talks with President Vladimir Putin in a year, more trilateral talks between the U.S., Ukraine and Russia are planned for later this month. While we’ve heard tales of imminent peace time and again, here's hoping American emissaries and their counterparts can finally bring an end to the fighting.That’s because, despite considerable efforts by the U.S. and Europe to help Ukraine win this war, there is no victory in sight. While Ukrainians arguably thwarted Russian advances in its very first weeks, its backers have failed to help Ukraine consolidate its battlefield victories at the negotiating table. As a result, Russia’s invasion has slowly wrecked Ukraine: the war is Europe's deadliest conflict since World War II and Russia has seized approximately a fifth of Ukraine’s territory . After years of needless death and destruction, what will it take to actually forge an agreement to finally end this war? articles.description: Airlines Face A "Reckoning" As Fuel Hedges Run Out With Jet Fuel Near $150 Authored by Irina Slav via OilPrice.com , Jet fuel is trading a little below $150 a barrel against about $85 before the war, and airline executives say it is staying there.  Hedges signed earlier this year are rolling off, so carriers must lock in today's prices or gamble on a slump, while winter cuts demand.  United CEO Scott Kirby expects six of 10 US airlines to lose money this year, and Europe's carriers have taken an extra $12 billion fuel hit, per The Telegraph. Reports about an oil glut are back in the media, and U.S. diesel just dropped below $6 per gallon. But these signs of normalization have yet to reach the airline industry, where jet fuel prices remain eye-wateringly high and hedging contracts are expiring. It seems not all airlines will survive the winter. Airlines have been among the sectors to feel the most immediate pain from the fallout of the war between the United States and Israel, and Iran. With jet fuel representing a solid portion of the industry's expenses, the fuel price jump following the squeeze on Hormuz tanker traffic immediately hit airlines. articles.title: Gensler Warns AI Bubble Will Burst Before 2028 As Warsh Reveals Fed Is Modeling A Crash
articles.description: Gensler Warns AI Bubble Will Burst Before 2028 As Warsh Reveals Fed Is Modeling A Crash Gary Gensler, who ran the SEC under Biden, says the AI boom is a bubble that will likely burst and push the US into recession before the 2028 presidential election. "It's already a bubble," Gensler told CNN in an interview published Monday, three days before Anthropic is due to start trading in what would be the largest IPO on record. Gensler, now a professor at MIT, pointed to estimates that as much as $800 billion a year is being poured into AI infrastructure, and said every great technology build-out of the past ended the same way. "History tells us that when you have a new technology and a significant investment...you come to a point where it plateaus. It retrenches," he said. "The only question is if it's a soft recession or something more dramatic." He listed the railroad boom, electricity in the 1920s and the internet in the 1990s as precedents, and put a date on this one: "I think we're going to have this repricing and a softening of the economy that happens before November 2028." articles.description: Lisa Cook Threatens To Skip Her Own Firing Hearing, Calls Trump's Panel A "Façade" Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook will not take part in the White House hearing that could end with President Trump firing her unless the administration replaces the panel and rewrites its rules , her lawyer Abbe Lowell told the White House in a letter dated Nov. 16 and made public on Tuesday. "Governor Cook has no legal obligation to participate in an unfair hearing," Lowell wrote to presidential counsel Will Scharf, adding that she "has a duty to the Federal Reserve to decline to participate in any proceeding" that would undermine the institution's independence. The three-member committee, he wrote, "appears to be a façade designed to obscure a predetermined decision to fire Governor Cook." Lowell went further, arguing that the president's "decision to fire Governor Cook has already been made" and that the committee exists "only to manufacture 'cause' for a predetermined removal outcome." According to DHS, Delon Raymond Jaundoo was arrested in Brooklyn on charges including attempted murder, first- and second-degree assault, criminal use of a firearm and multiple counts of criminal possession of a loaded weapon. New York City's Department of Correction declined to honor it and released him from Rikers. DHS says Jaundoo entered the country legally during the Obama administration and simply never left: his authorized stay ran out in January 2015 , more than 11 years ago. articles.title: ‘I have to sell my bum on OnlyFans to go on tour’: Kate Nash on fame, feminism and fighting the music business
articles.description: She threw a (metaphorical) brick through Spotify’s window and exposed industry failings with her ‘Butts for Tour Buses’ campaign. Now the singer is embracing her Irish roots with her new album’s fighting spirit Kate Nash was standing on a fire truck in a showgirl outfit complete with white tights and pink G-string, shouting through a loudhailer about the music industry’s failure to pay artists fairly, when she wondered if she’d gone too far. It was 2024 and the truck, which made pit stops outside the London offices of Spotify and Live Nation, had a large black-and-white picture of Nash’s bum on the back along with the words “Butts for Tour Buses” – a reference to her newly launched OnlyFans account, which she was using to fund her tour. That afternoon, she called her manager Kat. “I told her: ‘I’ve thrown a brick through the window at Spotify.’ She went: ‘What, literally?’ and I said: ‘No, but I’ve been standing outside their offices with a megaphone, so that relationship is over. I don’t think we’ll be making their New Music Friday feature.’ And we didn’t.” [see footnote] Continue reading...

articles.title: Blacklock, Birmingham B3: ‘A very, very cool version of an Angus Steakhouse’ – restaurant review
articles.description: Ever-open, eminently relatable, sensibly priced spots of this sort will always have an audience A London chophouse has taken up residence on St Philip’s Place, Birmingham, on the edge of Cathedral Square, or “Pigeon Park”, as the locals call it. This particular nook of Brum city centre is a magnet to those feathered blighters, although Blacklock ’s smoulderingly macho menu is ironically pigeon-meat free, revolving instead around heaps of chops and steaks cooked over charcoal. There’s porterhouse, bone-in sirloin, lamb rump and pig’s head on toast. Launched in London in 2015 , Blacklock was the elegant, edgy, no-nonsense dining experience for groovy young things who quite literally wanted meat and two veg, so long as said veg was dripping-fat chips; it now has five sites in the capital and another in Manchester. “We just ended up at Blacklock,” people used to tell me half a dozen times a week, then go on to rave about the bread, the gravy and the ash-baked sweet potatoes, and revel in the glorious simplicity of it all. articles.title: "It's Illegal": Trump Fires Back As Massive Leak Shows What Deutsche Bank Hid About Epstein, Russia - And Him
articles.description: "It's Illegal": Trump Fires Back As Massive Leak Shows What Deutsche Bank Hid About Epstein, Russia - And Him Deutsche Bank shares fell more than 6% in Frankfurt on Tuesday after 15 million leaked files showed the lender processed $582 million in suspicious payments tied to Jeffrey Epstein , quietly leaked Donald Trump's tax details to an outsider in 2017, and kept chasing Russian business right up to the invasion of Ukraine. More than 200 journalists at outlets including the Financial Times , Der Spiegel, Le Monde and the New York Times spent months on the cache, which two whistleblowers copied out of the bank and handed to Indian journalist Josy Joseph and South African journalist Khadija Sharife . articles.description: First Domino Falls: US AI Chip Crackdown Freezes $480MM Loan Linked To China's ByteDance As we discussed earlier, the Trump administration's move to tighten export controls on AI chips outside the US to ultimately restrict Chinese firms' access was met with anger and threats of retaliation from Beijing . The fallout is already underway and is now hitting financing: the new curbs have frozen work on a $480 million loan to fund Nvidia AI chips intended for ByteDance, Bloomberg reported this morning. Singapore-based Aolani Cloud Pte had been in discussions with banks about a loan to fund AI chips for a Malaysian data center, but the new restrictions have stalled those talks. Data center operators in countries including Singapore and Malaysia must now obtain licenses to purchase advanced AI chips. articles.description: Second Tanker In Two Days Sinks Off Bulgaria's Coast, As Black Sea War Heats Up While the tanker wars in the Strait of Hormuz have long been focus of international attention and headlines, a similar tanker war in the Black Sea has been ongoing . Recently the pace of major attacks and even sinkings against international vessels in the Black Sea has picked up, related to the war in Ukraine. Both sides have been going after the other's civilian imports and exports, claiming they have 'dual use' purposes and so can be targeted . via Defence Geek Over the last two days, two tankers have sunk off of Bulgaria's Black Sea coast. The country's defense ministry has announced that a Liberia-flagged gas tanker sank in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone after it disappeared from radar shortly after midnight . Its emergency buoy was activated, signaling rescuers that the ship has sunk. articles.title: Massive Cyberattack Turned 178 Of The World's Biggest Websites Against Their Own Visitors
articles.description: Massive Cyberattack Turned 178 Of The World's Biggest Websites Against Their Own Visitors Hackers spent most of Monday serving malware to visitors of 178 major organizations, including Zoom, CNN, Fox News, the BBC, HSBC, Equifax, Salesforce and IKEA, by hijacking a website-testing service those companies had all trusted with their pages. The malicious code rode in through Optimizely, a platform companies use to try out changes to their websites. According to Report URI , the security firm run by researcher Scott Helme that found it, the attacker planted JavaScript in the "Project JavaScript" field of Optimizely customer projects, so the poison was delivered from Optimizely's own servers - a domain the affected sites had already approved to run code in their visitors' browsers. This is a big one. We found malicious JavaScript being served through Optimizely to some of the world's largest websites. 178 organisations affected, with everything from crypto theft and card skimming to iOS exploits. articles.title: Judge Kills Trump Crackdown On 'Forever Students'
articles.description: Judge Kills Trump Crackdown On 'Forever Students' Authored by Aldgra Fredly via The Epoch Times , A federal judge on Nov. 16 vacated the Trump administration's final rule that would have limited how long foreign students can stay in the United States. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) issued the new rule in July to eliminate what the department described as the "'duration of status' loophole," which it said had allowed foreign students, exchange visitors, and media representatives to remain in the country indefinitely. The rule would have established fixed periods of stay for international students (F visas), exchange visitors (J visas), and representatives of foreign media (I visas). It would cap the length of stay for F and J visa holders in the United States at four years. U.S. District Judge F. Dennis Saylor IV of Massachusetts vacated the rule, finding it arbitrary and capricious because the department had failed to weigh the costs and benefits of implementing it. DHS had cited national security and fraud prevention as reasons for the change, but Saylor said they did not support the department's actions.
